connection_condition: Examination.ID carries the patient identifier and corresponds to Patient.ID; an examination record has no meaning without its patient.
description: A patient is composed of one or more clinical examination events. Linking the two tables is what allows patient demographics and diagnoses to be attached to an examination date.

connection_condition: Laboratory.ID carries the patient identifier and corresponds to Patient.ID; the Laboratory composite key is (ID, Date).
description: A patient is composed of one or more laboratory test events. Every laboratory record in this dataset resolves to a known patient.
Patient age is computed from the birthday, using the current date as the reference point; age has no stored column of its own.

connection_condition: Both columns draw on the same disease abbreviation vocabulary, but they are populated independently and use different spellings for Sjogren's syndrome (Patient.Diagnosis 'SJS' versus Examination.Diagnosis 'SjS').
description: The patient-level diagnosis and the examination-level diagnosis express the same business concept of 'which autoimmune disease does this patient have'; they differ in grain and completeness rather than in meaning.

connection_condition: Symptoms is populated exactly for the examinations whose Thrombosis grade is non-zero.
description: Observed symptoms and the thrombosis grade are recorded together: a non-empty Symptoms value is only present when a thrombosis grade other than 0 was assigned, so the two concepts co-occur on the same examination.

connection_condition: The two tables share only the patient identifier; there is no examination-level key linking a laboratory test date to an examination date.
description: Clinical examinations and laboratory tests are both patient-level clinical events collected on nearby but independently recorded dates. Any cross-analysis has to be made through the patient, not through a direct event key.
